The Medicine Creek Treaty, also known as the Treaty of Medicine Creek, is a significant treaty in the history of relations between the United States and the Native American tribes in the Pacific Northwest, including those in the area around Olympia, Washington. 

Signed on December 26, 1854, the Medicine Creek Treaty was one of several treaties negotiated by Washington Territory Governor Isaac Stevens with the tribes of the region. The treaty was signed by representatives of the Nisqually, Puyallup, Squaxin Island, and other tribes.

However, the interpretation and enforcement of treaty rights often depend on the specific language of the treaty, historical context, and subsequent legal and legislative actions. For instance, the Boldt Decision interpreted the phrase "in common with" in the fishing rights provisions of the treaties to mean that the tribes were entitled to up to 50% of the harvestable fish.

As we continue to grapple with these issues, it's crucial to approach them with a commitment to justice, respect for indigenous rights, and a willingness to learn from our shared history.

**Title:** Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Languages AI Legal Learning Module (IKSLLM)

**Executive Summary:**

The consortium of professors and alumni from Evergreen State College, in collaboration with [Tribal Affiliations], proposes to develop an AI Legal Learning Module (LLM) trained on indigenous languages and indigenous knowledge systems. This project will leverage the open-source repositories of Hugging Face and build upon a proof of concept using contexting systems for ChatGPT-4. The proposed AI LLM will address the critical need for legal technology that respects and incorporates indigenous perspectives, languages, and legal traditions.

**Project Description:**

The IKSLLM project aims to create an AI system that can understand and interpret indigenous languages and knowledge systems, with a particular focus on legal contexts. This system will be trained on a diverse range of data sources, including tribal treaties, case law, and other legal documents, as well as oral histories, traditional stories, and other forms of indigenous knowledge. The system will be designed to assist in legal research, education, and decision-making, providing a valuable tool for indigenous communities, legal professionals, scholars, and policymakers.

**Methodology:**

The project will use the Hugging Face open-source libraries as a foundation, building upon the existing capabilities of the ChatGPT-4 model. The model will be retrained using a dataset compiled from indigenous languages and knowledge systems. This will involve collaboration with indigenous communities and experts to ensure the accuracy, respectfulness, and cultural appropriateness of the data collection and training process.

**Budget:**

| Item | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Data collection and preparation | $50,000 |
| Model training and development | $100,000 |
| Testing and validation | $30,000 |
| Project management and administration | $20,000 |
| Collaboration and consultation with indigenous communities and experts | $50,000 |
| Dissemination and outreach | $10,000 |
| Contingency (10%) | $26,000 |
| **Total** | **$286,000** |

**Timeline:**

The project is expected to take 24 months, with the following milestones:

- Months 1-6: Data collection and preparation
- Months 7-12: Model training and development
- Months 13-18: Testing and validation
- Months 19-24: Dissemination and outreach

**Expected Outcomes:**

The IKSLLM project will result in an AI system capable of understanding and interpreting indigenous languages and knowledge systems in legal contexts. This will provide a valuable tool for indigenous communities, legal professionals, scholars, and policymakers, and will contribute to the broader recognition and respect for indigenous rights and legal traditions.

**Evaluation:**

The project will be evaluated based on the accuracy and usefulness of the AI system, as well as the quality of the collaboration with indigenous communities and experts. Feedback from users and stakeholders will be collected and used to improve the system and guide future work.

**Conclusion:**

The IKSLLM project represents a significant opportunity to advance the field of legal technology and contribute to the recognition and respect for indigenous rights and legal traditions. We look forward to the possibility of working with [Granting Agency] to make this vision a reality.
